newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa leaves hospital at own request.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa leaves hospital at own request.

text.p: Mother Teresa was released from hospital at her own request on Friday after fighting heart problems and malaria for nearly three weeks.

The 86-year-old Nobel peace laureate, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her work with the poor and destitute, was taken by wheelchair and ambulance to her Calcutta home from the Woodland's Nursing Home, where she was admitted on August 20.

"We had a plan to release her on Saturday but she was restless and wanted to go home today. We could not force her to stay one more day," Dr S.K. Sen, the nursing home's medical director, told reporters.
"She is a little stronger but she needs lots of rest," he added.
Dr A.K. Bardhan, one of six doctors attending the Roman Catholic nun, who has had a heart pacemaker since 1989, said: "We have discharged her on her own request."
As she left hospital, Mother Teresa thanked doctors for all they had done for her. "May God bless you," she said.
She had been admitted to hospital with malaria and mild pneumonia and suffered heart failure while in intensive care.
Mother Teresa's stay in hospital attracted international attention as members of her Calcutta-based religious order, Missionaries of Charity, held round-the-clock prayers for her recovery.
She was taken from the hospital, where doctors said she had suffered two heart attacks, by wheelchair to an ambulance which drove her to the Mother House, headquarters of the Missionaries of Charity.
Her room at the Mother House, in a busy central Calcutta area, had been equipped with artificial respiratory equipment, doctors said.
The sisters of her charity held welcome prayers for her at the Mother House. "We are happy that mother is back," one sister said.
Mother Teresa has spent much of her life surrounded by the sick, the destitute and the dying.
The Missionaries of Charity, which she founded in 1949, runs some 544 homes for unwanted children and the destitute in more than 80 cities.
The work includes the care of nearly 7,000 children in 120 homes and arranging 1,500 adoptions each year.
In 1991, Mother Teresa was treated at a Californian hospital for heart disease and bacterial pneumonia.
Two years later, she fell in Rome and broke three ribs. In August 1993, she developed malaria, complicated by her heart and lung problems. Last April, she fractured her left collar bone.
Mother Teresa was born Agnes Goinxha Bejaxhiu to Albanian parents in Skopje, in what was then Serbia, on August 27, 1910.
